---
title: "Reading the outputs"
subtitle: "Collections, native responses, metric sets, and their provenance"
---

Run products live under the configured `project_dir`. For production projects,
use a directory outside the toolbox checkout.

## The layout

```text
<project_dir>/
  config/runs/                   configuration records and invocation history
  data/spatial/                  basin geometry, locations and maps
  data/climate/                  historical forcing and projection products
  models/hydrology/wflow/         model, historical run and evaluation
  scenario_plans/<request_id>/    exact generation selection and staging
  scenario_collections/<id>/      immutable collection
    collection.json              readiness marker and inventory
    scenario_table.csv           explicit run membership and ancestry
    stress_test_lookup.csv       monthly perturbation parameters
    forcing/run_<run_id>.nc       durable generated forcing
    preparation_context.json     portable adapter declaration
    preparation_catalog.yml      reduced HydroMT catalog
    ancillary/                   packaged preparation inputs
  experiments/<name>/
    config/simulation.json       frozen simulation identity
    hydrology/wflow/output/      retained native responses
    responses/response_inventory.json
    results/metric_plans/        response-dependent metric selection
    results/metric_sets/<id>/
      metrics.json              readiness marker and provenance
      unit_index.csv            run and bundle membership
      metric_environment.json   resolved stage dependencies
      return_level_benchmark.json  the return-level estimator's evidence
      <token>_indicators.csv     metric,location,unit_id,value
  logs/
  benchmarks/
```

Two experiments can consume the same collection. Their native responses and
metric sets remain scoped to their own experiment. Never infer membership from
filenames: join textual `unit_id` through `unit_index.csv` to the scenario table.
The empty stochastic `st_id` is the unperturbed scenario, outside the surface.

## Logs and benchmarks

WF0, WF1 and WF2 retain their project-level merged logs. Generation uses
`logs/wf3_generate_scenarios_<request_id>.log`; simulation uses
`logs/wf4_simulate_system_<experiment>.log`. Parts are separated under
`logs/_parts/generate_scenarios/<request_id>/` and
`logs/_parts/simulate_system/<experiment>/`. Benchmark parts use the same
scoping beneath `benchmarks/_parts/`.

The runners record invocations under `config/runs/invocations/`, including
failure and dry-run outcomes. An invocation record describes execution; it does
not make an incomplete collection or metric set ready.

## Reading a metric set

Read the selected metric set's `metrics.json` before its tables. It records
metric declarations, response identity, environment, resolved references and
exact expected keys. Missing, duplicate or extra keys are validation failures.

Class-A metrics have one value per run. Class-B fits belong to explicit bundles.
Class-C wet/dry-month values have one value per run at a shared reference month;
the manifest records the reference gauge and members. Values retain the existing
four-significant-digit format. Return-level qualification and limitations are
recorded alongside the results.

## Return levels and their evidence

Class-B return levels are fitted with a range-normalized sample L-moment GEV
estimator (`gf15-lmoments-c/1`). Each set records what backs that fit:

- `return_level_validation` in `metrics.json` — the closed declaration: the
  policy, the screening settings, the exact tested domain, and the criteria.
- `return_level_benchmark.json` — the benchmark report those criteria come
  from, copied into the set so it stays readable without the installed
  toolbox. The declaration carries its digest; a set whose report is missing or
  altered is refused rather than read as unassessed.
- `return_level_evidence` — per location, the usable-block counts and coverage,
  the fitted parameters, and the retained fit record with its reached stages.

Read the declaration before the numbers. It is deliberately narrow: the
benchmark is a bounded assessment on synthetic fixtures at the two production
probabilities, re-scored against owner-selected relaxed limits on data that had
already been observed. It states `application_scope: operational_screen_only`,
`actual_bundle_applicability: unestablished` and `screening_policy_validated:
false`. Return levels are first-order screening values with no uncertainty
interval, not validated design estimates, and a bounded declaration is never
widened to cover a return period it did not test — asking for one aborts the
run instead.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A detached indicators CSV cannot tell you which estimator produced it

The four-column `<token>_indicators.csv` carries metric names and values and
nothing about provenance. Metric names did **not** change when the estimator
did, so a CSV copied out of its metric set is indistinguishable from one
produced by the previous estimator, and two vintages will merge silently and
wrongly.

When you compare or archive results, keep the whole metric set: the table, its
`metrics.json`, the `return_level_benchmark.json` beside it, and the retained
responses they were reduced from. Never infer the estimator from a file name, a
metric name or the CSV schema.
:::

## Are these outputs current?

Routine simulation validates its exact generation plan against current inputs.
A missing or stale plan names the generation command needed to repair it;
simulation never generates a collection or chooses the latest directory.
An explicit collection manifest permits independent reuse with its packaged
preparation inputs.

An experiment's frozen simulation record binds the collection, model and
simulator settings. Changed simulation inputs require a new experiment name.
Changing only metrics creates a new immutable metric set from retained responses.
`operation: metrics-only` needs no live model, generation data or Julia.

WF1 and WF2 retain configuration digests in their run records and result
sidecars. For WF1, `models/hydrology/wflow/hydromt_build_config.yml` records the
settings actually passed to HydroMT. Configuration provenance alone does not
establish scientific data identity; collection and response manifests carry the
corresponding content records.
